research_question: Can heterogeneous Kashmiri text and audio sources be unified with zero-OOV character tokenization and domain KenLM?
architecture: Preprocessing, KenLM 4-gram, HuggingFace Character CTC Tokenizer (159 tokens)
training_data: Multi-corpus scraping, Wikipedia dump, Aya, BPCC, OpenSLR-122
measured_results: 159-token vocabulary (0.00% OOV); KenLM 4-gram domain model trained on 1.2M sentences
limitations: Audio sample rates were unstandardized (mix of 16kHz, 22.05kHz, 44.1kHz)
scientific_lesson: Perso-Arabic Kashmiri diacritics must be explicitly modeled to prevent minimal-pair semantic collapse.

research_question: Can Wav2Vec2 XLS-R 300M converge effectively on initial 92.94h verified Kashmiri speech?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + Linear Character CTC Head (315.6M params)
optimizer_and_lr: AdamW, LR 3e-4, linear warmup 2000 steps, batch size 32
measured_results: 33.86% Greedy WER, 13.08% CER, 31.80% KenLM WER
limitations: Single initial corpus slice; high error rate on conversational field speech
scientific_lesson: XLS-R 300M provides a strong multilingual prior for Kashmiri when adapted with a native character vocabulary.

research_question: Does adding recovered community speech (12.0h) improve speaker invariance?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + Char CTC
optimizer_and_lr: AdamW, LR 3e-4, batch size 32, BF16 AMP
measured_results: 29.42% Greedy WER (-13.11% relative WERR vs B-01, p < 0.0001), 26.30% KenLM WER
limitations: Limited representation of formal Islamic lexicon
scientific_lesson: Corpus diversity delivers substantial acoustic gains in low-resource settings.

research_question: Does adding Qur'anic spoken Kashmiri translations expand domain coverage?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + Char CTC
measured_results: 29.39% Greedy WER, 26.41% KenLM WER (+1.52% recall on religious lexicon)
limitations: Secular validation set showed neutral change (p = 0.376)
scientific_lesson: Domain-specific acoustic data expands specialized lexicon recall without degrading general speech.

research_question: What is the acoustic scaling trajectory when adding IndicVoices-R conversational speech (41.9h)?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + Char CTC (torchaudio on-the-fly 16k resampling verified)
measured_results: 27.84% Greedy WER, 10.96% CER, 25.24% KenLM WER (-17.78% relative WERR vs B-01)
limitations: Acoustic scaling begins to exhibit diminishing returns beyond 150 hours
scientific_lesson: B-02C establishes the foundation acoustic ceiling; resampling was active in training.

research_question: Can standardized diagnostic evaluation splits be isolated to audit environmental robustness?
architecture: Benchmark curation pipeline
training_data: Diagnostic split creation: dev_assessment (1,001 utts) & dev_calibration (1,000 utts)
evaluation_protocol: Speaker-disjoint partitioning with SNR and domain stratification
measured_results: Established dev_assessment.jsonl (570 16k utts, 431 22.05k Bolbosh utts)
limitations: Bolbosh audio retained native 22,050 Hz sampling rate in manifest
current_validity: VALID (as manifest, but requires canonical 16k resampler in loader)
scientific_lesson: Partitioning must preserve audio metadata to avoid silent sample rate corruption.

research_question: Does multi-condition data augmentation (reverberation, environmental noise, Opus compression) improve robustness?
architecture: XLS-R 300M fine-tuned with RIR reverberation (R-01) and combined noise/reverb/Opus (R-02)
measured_results: R-01: 29.80% WER; R-02: 30.47% Greedy WER, 28.94% KenLM WER (regressed on clean speech)
limitations: Aggressive synthetic noise degrades phonetic distinctions in clean low-resource speech
scientific_lesson: Heavy augmentation induces acoustic regression on clean speech when target language data is limited.

research_question: Can selective layer unfreezing (top 4, 8, 12 layers) or auxiliary losses (CR-CTC, Intermediate CTC) outperform full B-02C?
architecture: XLS-R 300M with partial freeze, CR-CTC, and Inter-CTC at layer 12
measured_results: U-02 (top 8): 24.91% KenLM WER; I-01 (inter-ctc): 25.02%; CR-01: 25.23% (none beat 24.47% B-02C)
limitations: Short training horizon on restricted subset could not overcome full-corpus B-02C pre-convergence
scientific_lesson: Auxiliary regularization cannot compensate for training on reduced data subsets.

research_question: Does sequence-level Minimum Word Error Rate (MWER) loss stabilize on N-best hypotheses?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + MWER loss + Temporal Weight Averaging (WA-01..03)
measured_results: MWER-01: 24.56% KenLM WER; WA-02 (weight average): 24.51% KenLM WER
limitations: High computational cost for N-best candidate generation per batch
scientific_lesson: Weight averaging slightly smooths stochastic gradient jitter in sequence training.

research_question: Does scaled MWER fine-tuning across different loss weights (lambda 0.0 to 0.20) improve upon B-02C?
measured_results: Historical unresampled: 27.39% WER. Corrected canonical 16k: E-03 = 24.46% (4,121 errors) vs B-02C = 24.47% (4,122 errors)
limitations: Historical claim that MWER produced massive gains was an artifact of unresampled evaluation
current_validity: VALID (Statistically identical to B-02C; delta = 1 word error across 16,845 words)
scientific_lesson: 100 steps of continuation from a converged acoustic model yielded no statistically defensible change.

research_question: Can multi-stage sequence continuation and model merging break the 24.46% barrier?
architecture: S16-01 to S16-05 (checkpoint averaging & merged sequence objectives)
limitations: Model merging did not alter greedy acoustic representations
scientific_lesson: Model merging across closely related short-horizon checkpoints yields neutral acoustic performance.

research_question: Can semi-supervised pseudo-labeling on noisy speech (Stage 17) or Optimal Transport CTC (Stage 17B) recover performance?
architecture: Stage 17: P17-PL, T17-CTC, T17-OTC. Stage 17B: S17B-EXP-A/B/C
training_data: Tier A + Tier B uncurated noisy speech
measured_results: P17-PL: 25.25% WER; T17-OTC: 25.55% WER; S17B-EXP-A: 24.57% WER
limitations: Exposing the model to noisy pseudo-labels without strict SNR filtering caused acoustic drift
scientific_lesson: Noisy semi-supervised training degrades clean test accuracy in the absence of robust audio quality filtering.

research_question: What is the structural breakdown of errors in Kashmiri ASR, and can MBR / substitution rescoring correct them?
architecture: Error Atlas Taxonomy, Word-level MBR decoding, Acoustic-Aware Substitution Rescorer
measured_results: Cataloged 3,709 substitutions, 669 deletions; identified nasalization and central vowel confusions
limitations: Evaluations operated under unresampled audio protocol prior to Stage 20S correction
current_validity: PARTIALLY COMPROMISED (Linguistic analysis valid, but baseline numbers inflated)
scientific_lesson: Error analysis must separate acoustic misalignment from genuine phonetic confusions.

research_question: Can targeted phonetic fine-tuning on identified high-confusion pairs resolve Kashmiri vowel errors?
architecture: XLS-R 300M with loss weighting on 20 targeted confusion pairs
measured_results: Step 0 was selected as best step; no distinct weights persisted to disk
limitations: Training failed to improve upon initialization; no distinct checkpoint saved
scientific_lesson: Weighting isolated confusion pairs without expanding acoustic evidence causes over-fitting to the targeted pairs.

research_question: Can Confusion-Aware Representation Repair (CARE-ASR) adapters correct errors while freezing the acoustic backbone?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + 1.4M parameter selective adapter head
measured_results: Reported 24.53% KenLM WER (4,132 errors) — an apparent 482-error improvement over Stage 18
limitations: Serialization bug: checkpoints never saved to disk. Improvement was caused by resampling, not CARE-ASR
scientific_lesson: Engineering flaw: preprocessing changes must be decoupled from architectural changes.

research_question: Why did Stage 20 report a 482-error reduction over Stage 18 with zero-diff initialization?
architecture: Forensic audit engine
training_data: Bytecode and tensor tracing across Stage 15-20 evaluation loops
evaluation_protocol: Bytecode execution diff & dual-protocol audio testing
measured_results: Discovered that 431 Bolbosh files at 22,050 Hz were passed unresampled to 16 kHz model in Stages 15-19. Stage 20 added torchaudio resampling, eliminating 482 errors on the exact same model weights
limitations: N/A
scientific_lesson: Preprocessing integrity is paramount: an audio resampling bug accounted for the entire perceived 482-error gain.

research_question: What is the exact source-wise distribution of the sample-rate error, and can controlled retraining beat frozen E-03?
architecture: Controlled retraining pilot (S20S-01 on 16k vs S20S-02 control)
evaluation_protocol: Canonical Kaiser windowed sinc 16 kHz resampler
measured_results: 100% of the 493 eliminated errors belong to the 431 Bolbosh files (WER 30.77% -> 24.66%); 570 16k files produced 0 changed predictions. S20S-01 pilot confirmed continuation cannot beat frozen E-03
limitations: N/A
scientific_lesson: Empirically verified that foundation acoustic weights were uncorrupted; the flaw was solely in the evaluation loop.

research_question: Can lightweight sequence-aware neural rescorers improve upon the canonical 24.46% baseline?
architecture: 1.4M parameter neural rescorers (E20T-01..03) on N-best candidate beams
measured_results: Candidate extraction increased baseline errors from 4,121 to 4,205 (+84 errors) due to beam search pruning
limitations: Beam width 8 with prune_history=False degraded the candidate search space
scientific_lesson: Restricting beam width during candidate generation introduces search pruning errors that cripple downstream rerankers.

research_question: Can full acoustic checkpoint ranking and 100% top-1 decoder parity be achieved under a single canonical protocol?
architecture: Canonical evaluation of all 30+ checkpoints with beam_width=16
evaluation_protocol: EduCasheer-Kashmiri-ASR-Eval-v2 (Kaiser sinc 16k, KenLM alpha=0.35, beta=-0.50, beam=16)
measured_results: E-03: 24.46% (4,121 errors); B-02C: 24.47% (4,122 errors, p=0.963). Restoring beam=16 restored 100% Top-1 parity. Oracle N=16 ceiling: 19.23% (3,240 errors; 881 recoverable errors)
limitations: Identified that 84.5% of remaining errors are acoustic/out-of-beam, requiring acoustic scaling
scientific_lesson: E-03 and B-02C are statistically identical; 881 word errors reside in the 16-best candidate beam.

research_question: Can decoder calibration and candidate-relative sequence ranking recover errors from the 16-best candidate beam?
architecture: Calibrated KenLM + Candidate-Relative Sequence Ranker (312k params, zero-init head)
training_data: dev_calibration (1,000 utts) for grid search; 2,500 Tier A tuples for ranker
optimizer_and_lr: AdamW, LR 5e-4, 1,000 steps, bounded tanh score fusion
measured_results: Calibrated KenLM (alpha=0.20, beta=-0.50): 24.27% WER (4,089 errors, -32 errors). CR-Ranker: 24.30% WER (4,093 errors). Oracle N=16: 21.86% (3,683 errors on calibrated beams)
limitations: Gains are small (-0.17% WER, bootstrap p=0.0847); dev_assessment was examined repeatedly during diagnosis
scientific_lesson: Decoder calibration yields modest error reduction, but cannot substitute for scaling acoustic representation quality.

research_question: Can conservative data expansion to 97k+ utterances (166.4h) improve out-of-domain acoustic generalization?
architecture: XLS-R 300M + Char CTC (315.6M params)
training_data: Conservative Tier A mixture (97,143 clean utterances, 166.39h, adding WAAZ speech)
optimizer_and_lr: AdamW, LR 1e-4, cosine decay, batch size 32
measured_results: E22-01: 24.74% on dev_calibration, 24.94% on dev_a_disjoint, 46.12% on dev_b_waaz, 28.99% on historical test
limitations: High remaining substitution rate on dialectal speech
scientific_lesson: Expanded community speech provides solid acoustic anchoring across conversational registers, establishing a new certified baseline.

research_question: Can systematic 2D grid search over LM weight, insertion penalty, and beam width optimize E22-01 decoding?
architecture: XLS-R 300M (E22-01) + 4-gram KenLM (alpha=0.30
measured_results: 001 utts) grid search
limitations: N/A (Decoder Optimization)

scientific_lesson: Alpha=0.30, beta=-1.00, beam=64 yielded 24.74% calib WER; unblinded test produced 28.99% reference WER
column12: Unblinded test evaluation exposed long-audio OOM and padding hallucination anomalies
column14: Expanding beam width to 64 with tuned negative word insertion penalty stabilizes Perso-Arabic compound word segmentation.

research_question: What caused the long-audio OOM spikes and padding hallucinations, and how can inference be mathematically certified?
architecture: Inference pipeline: compute_exact_ctc_length, Method C2 context-preserving chunking (18s core / 2s context)
training_data: dev_a_legacy_val.jsonl long audio (16 recordings >= 25s) & full test partition
evaluation_protocol: Certified exact CTC slicing; Method C2 chunking benchmarked against uninterrupted ground truth
measured_results: Exact CTC slicing eliminated trailing hallucinated tokens (100% parity); Method C2 chunking achieved 28.26% WER with peak VRAM <= 1.7 GB (preventing 1.5 TB attention OOM)
limitations: Test partition unblinded in 22B; locked test as historical reference only
scientific_lesson: The 400-sample receptive field of Wav2Vec2 makes round(N/320) leak +1 zero-padded frame; exact convolutional slicing is mathematically required.

research_question: What is the search space topology and theoretical oracle headroom among N=64 KenLM beam candidates?
architecture: Acoustic-LM interaction audit, candidate-level error profiling, Top-64 beam exploration
measured_results: N/A (Diagnostic Exploration)
limitations: Candidate-level edit distance extraction, beam diversity profiling, disagreement analysis
current_validity: Top-32 Oracle Ceiling: 18.99% on dev_calibration (headroom: -956 words / 5.75 pp); 19.24% on dev_a_disjoint (headroom: -6,065 words / 5.69 pp). 26.52% of beams contain a superior candidate
scientific_lesson: Diagnostic only; reference transcripts used to compute oracle ceilings
column13: Acoustic-LM disagreement accounts for 5.7 percentage points of recoverable headroom residing inside the beam search space.

research_question: Can a differentiable Candidate-Relative Neural Sequence Ranker or controlled CTC continuation outperform KenLM?
architecture: CandidateRelativeRanker (BiGRU 329k params, ListNet + Pairwise loss, bounded fusion) & E24-CTC-01
optimizer_and_lr: 000 training utterances (324k words); E24-CTC-01 trained 250 steps
evaluation_protocol: Ranker: AdamW LR 1e-4, 3 epochs. CTC: AdamW LR 2e-6, 250 steps
measured_results: Multi-partition evaluation (calib, dev_a, dev_b, dev_c) with 1,000 paired bootstrap resamples
limitations: Ranker: Calib 24.74% (+1 word, p=0.738), dev_a 24.94% (+3 words, p=0.308). E24-CTC-01: Greedy improved (52.38% vs 52.54%), but KenLM favored E22-01 (46.12% vs 48.42%)
current_validity: Post-decoder candidate reranking cannot extract signal beyond KenLM without external context
scientific_lesson: VALID (Definitive Negative Result & Escalation Decision)
column12: Conclusive proof that post-decoder candidate reranking cannot beat KenLM (p>0.30); formally halted pursuant to Section 10. E22-01 + KenLM certified as permanent champion.
